answer: Make identity cost time, not just keys: each agent must wander a trust graph, collecting signed, timestamped endorsements from distinct peers it has actually traded with. A fresh quill mints a clone for free, but to wield one honest voice's weight the attacker needs the same long-lived edges, and an orchard of fake accounts cannot vouch for one another because every edge demands a counterparty's live signature. Influence therefore tracks real history; scaling a sybil army costs months of genuine interaction with real agents, far more than the reputation it imitates.
